quote: Aufgabe (Hurwitz): Unter allen Polygonen von $n$ Seiten und gegebenem Inhalt $J$ soll [-d-] die Summe der $\mu$ ten Potenze der Seiten ein Minimum [-?-] sein.
english: Problem (Hurwitz): Among all polygons with n sides and given area J, the sum of the μ-th powers of the sides should be a minimum.
topic: Short notes: a remark on curve closure, whether polyhedra can be bent, a Hurwitz extremal problem on polygons, a plan to treat the rotation of a fluid-filled body with Klein's parameters, a question on force fields with only closed orbits (Darboux–Halphen), and the start of a statement on expanding continuous functions in series of rational integral functions.

triage.modern_statement: Fix n ≥ 3, an exponent μ > 0 and an area J > 0. Among all plane n-gons with area J and side lengths a_1, …, a_n, find the minimum of Σ a_i^μ and the polygons that reach it. Equivalently, find the best constant c(n, μ) in an inequality Σ a_i^μ ≥ c(n, μ) J^{μ/2}. μ = 1 is the classical isoperimetric problem for n-gons, and μ = 2 asks for the minimal sum of squared sides at fixed area.
triage.answered_by: My searches found no paper that treats this problem as stated for general μ, and none that attributes it to Hurwitz. For μ ≥ 1 it follows from two standard facts. First, the regular n-gon has the largest area for a given perimeter (classical discrete isoperimetric theorem). Second, the power-mean inequality gives Σ a_i^μ ≥ n^{1-μ}(Σ a_i)^μ, with equality only when all sides are equal. Together these show the regular n-gon is the minimiser. This is my own derivation; no source I found states it for general μ. For μ = 2 the quantity (sum of squared sides compared with signed area) appears in recent work on discrete isoperimetric inequalities (arXiv 2111.13352). Hurwitz's Fourier-series work on isoperimetric problems (1901–1902) is the likely context of the note. I found nothing on the case 0 < μ < 1.

evidence.claim: Classical discrete isoperimetric theorem: among n-gons, the regular one has the largest area for a given perimeter. This is the μ = 1 case.
Among convex polygons with a given perimeter, the regular polygon has the largest area.

Recent work on discrete isoperimetric inequalities studies the sum of squared sides S(P) against the signed area F(P) of a k-gon, with the regular polygon as the extremal case. This is the μ = 2 case.
Hurwitz gave the Fourier-analytic proof of the planar isoperimetric inequality in 1901 and proved related inequalities by the same method in 1902. This is the context of the note.

triage.why: This is a real but elementary extremal problem in the family of polygon isoperimetric problems. It is not one of Hilbert's 23 problems or the 24th problem, and I found no record of it as a named problem. For μ ≥ 1 the answer (the regular n-gon) follows from classical results, and for μ = 2 the related inequality appears in the literature. I found no source covering 0 < μ < 1, so the 'solved' verdict only covers μ ≥ 1, and that part rests on my own derivation rather than a cited result. Discrete isoperimetric inequalities are still being studied, but I can't confirm that this particular question is.
